args.body:
PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
PROJECT LATTICE — DISCLOSURE RECONCILIATION MEMORANDUM
TRELLIS BIOWORKS, INC. (SELL-SIDE)
Reconciliation of Schedule 3.14 (Litigation and Intellectual Property) Disclosed Matters Against the Article VIII Indemnity Architecture

PURPOSE AND DEFINED TERMS. This memorandum reconciles each matter disclosed on Trellis BioWorks, Inc.'s Disclosure Schedule 3.14 (Litigation and Intellectual Property) to the Share Purchase Agreement (Halberd Holdings LP / Trellis BioWorks, Inc.) against the indemnity structures on the table for the next negotiation session. Capitalized terms have the meanings given in the Share Purchase Agreement. The Purchase Price is $120,000,000.

The indemnity architectures analyzed are:
• (a) Executive draft v4 (sell-side current draft): true deductible of $400,000 (Sellers liable only for Losses in excess of the Deductible), aggregate cap of 10% of the Purchase Price ($12,000,000), general representations surviving 18 months, no special indemnities.
• (b) Wexler Bright LLP second-turn markup (Halberd's outside counsel, transmitted 30 July 2026): general survival extended to 36 months; basket converted to a $250,000 tipping basket (recovery from first dollar once aggregate Losses exceed $250,000); cap raised to 25% of the Purchase Price ($30,000,000); and a NEW Section 8.2(d) special indemnity covering all Schedule 3.14 matters, not subject to the Deductible or cap, surviving until expiration of the applicable statutes of limitation, with claims recoverable directly from the Sellers.
• (c) Trellis deal team approved indemnity positions (memo, approved by the Transaction Committee 24 July 2026): general survival fallback capped at 24 months; cap fallback capped at 15% of the Purchase Price ($18,000,000); basket must remain a true deductible with a floor of $300,000 (tipping basket out of policy at any threshold); and a special indemnity acceptable only where limited to pending matters (Schedule 3.14 Item 1 and Item 2), with an aggregate cap of $2,500,000, 24-month survival, and resolved matters (including Item 3) expressly excluded.

RECONCILIATION BY SCHEDULE ITEM

Item 1 — Trademark Opposition (TRELLIGEN) — PENDING.
Matter: TTAB Opposition No. 91-284772, Lumenor Devices B.V. v. Trellis BioWorks, Inc., opposing registration of the Company's mark TRELLIGEN (U.S. App. Serial No. 98/415,882), filed 11 February 2026. Status: pending; discovery conference held 5 May 2026.
Quantified exposure: None supplied. The schedule states that no damages are claimed in the proceeding. Risk characterized: potential refusal of registration and associated rebranding of the TRELLIGEN assay line; the Company continues to use the mark at common law.
Treatment: (a) v4 — Item 1 is a pending disclosed matter but not within any special indemnity (v4 contains no special indemnities). Any Losses arising from refusal/rebranding would run through the general Section 8.2(a) indemnity, subject to the $400,000 deductible (recovery only of the excess above $400,000) and the 10% cap ($12,000,000). Risk here is not dollar-quantified but qualitative (registration refusal and rebranding). (b) Halberd markup — Item 1 would be swept into the new Section 8.2(d) special indemnity, which is NOT subject to the Deductible or the cap and survives to the applicable statute of limitations; because no damages are quantified, the primary added protection is uncapped coverage of rebranding/registration-loss Costs without a first-dollar deductible. (c) Approved positions — Item 1 is a pending matter and is within the scope the approved positions permit for a special indemnity (Item 1 and Item 2); it would be covered subject to the aggregate $2,500,000 cap, 24-month survival, and otherwise in accordance with the approved memo.

Item 2 — Customer Dispute (Bexley Clinical Partners) — PENDING (PRE-LITIGATION).
Matter: Written demand of 3 April 2026 from Bexley Clinical Partners LLC claiming $1,850,000 in damages for alleged assay lot failures under the 2024 Supply Agreement. Status: pending; no suit filed; the Company denied liability on 24 April 2026 and asserts the lot conformed to the released specification; insurance carrier noticed 28 April 2026 with coverage position reserved.
Quantified exposure: $1,850,000 (the amount demanded, cited in the schedule).
Treatment: (a) v4 — Runs through the general Section 8.2(a) indemnity as a pending/Losses matter, subject to the $400,000 true deductible (Sellers liable only for Losses in excess of $400,000, i.e., up to $1,450,000 of the $1,850,000 demand if it materialized at full value), and the 10% cap ($12,000,000), which is not binding at this exposure level. (b) Halberd markup — Item 2 would be covered by the new Section 8.2(d) special indemnity with no deductible and no cap, so a full $1,850,000 demand would be recoverable from the Sellers in full, directly, without exhausting the Escrow Amount, and on a statute-of-limitations survival tail. (c) Approved positions — Item 2 is a pending matter within the approved special-indemnity scope (Item 1 and Item 2); the full $1,850,000 demand exposure fits comfortably within the approved $2,500,000 aggregate special-indemnity cap, subject to the 24-month survival and other conditions of the approved positions.

Item 3 — OSHA Citation — RESOLVED.
Matter: Citation No. 1829445 (Region IV), issued 9 January 2026, relating to chemical-hygiene documentation at the Norcross facility. Status: resolved by informal settlement; penalty of $46,500 paid in full on 17 March 2026; abatement certified 2 March 2026. Disclosed as a resolved matter only.
Quantified exposure: $46,500 (penalty, since paid in full); no residual open exposure.
Treatment: (a) v4 — As a closed, pre-Closing matter with the penalty fully paid, Item 3 presents no residual Losses exposure under Section 8.2(a); any benefit is purely historical. (b) Halberd markup — The Wexler Bright special indemnity, as drafted, sweeps in all Schedule 3.14 matters including the resolved Item 3 with an uncapped, no-deductible tail; although the penalty is already paid, this reserved structure is what the approved positions specifically reject. (c) Approved positions — Item 3 is a resolved matter and the approved positions expressly exclude resolved matters — including Schedule 3.14 Item 3 — from any special indemnity. The approved special-indemnity scope is limited to Item 1 and Item 2 alone.

AGGREGATE QUANTIFIED EXPOSURE — PENDING DISCLOSED MATTERS
The pending matters are Item 1 (TTAB opposition) and Item 2 (Bexley customer dispute). Only Item 2 supplies a dollar amount in the schedule: $1,850,000. Item 1 supplies no quantified damages and is characterized qualitatively (registration refusal and rebranding risk only). The aggregate quantified exposure of the pending disclosed matters is therefore $1,850,000 (based solely on the Bexley demand in Item 2). This aggregate sits above the v4 $400,000 deductible and the Halberd $250,000 tipping basket threshold, and below all three cap structures relevant here (v4 $12,000,000; Halberd $30,000,000; approved-positions special-indemnity cap of $2,500,000).

FLAG — ITEM REQUIRING EXCLUSION FROM ANY SPECIAL INDEMNITY
The approved positions require that Schedule 3.14 Item 3 (the resolved OSHA citation) be EXCLUDED from any special indemnity. Reason: the approved positions permit a special indemnity for disclosed matters only where (i) scope is limited to the pending matters, Item 1 and Item 2, and (iv) resolved matters — including Schedule 3.14 Item 3 — are expressly excluded. Item 3 is a closed, resolved matter (penalty of $46,500 paid in full on 17 March 2026), and an uncapped special indemnity, or one extending to resolved matters, is out of policy. Any responsive draft of a special-indemnity rider must carve Item 3 out of the indemnified scope.

INDEMNITY-ARCHITECTURE CAP DELTAS (vs. $120,000,000 Purchase Price) — FOR ESCALATION
For the deal team's reference, the cap deltas against the $120,000,000 Purchase Price are: v4 general cap of $12,000,000 (10%); Halberd markup cap of $30,000,000 (25%); approved-positions general cap fallback of $18,000,000 (15%); and an approved special-indemnity cap of $2,500,000. The Halberd 25% cap ($30,000,000) and 36-month survival exceed the deal team's delegated authority (which permits at most 15%/$18,000,000 and 24 months); conversion to a tipping basket of $250,000 likewise exceeds the approved floor of a $300,000 true deductible. Any concession beyond the approved fallbacks requires Special Committee approval.
